name: CI — Server and Credentials Already in the Environment
query: List the registered workflows and fail the job if `order_pipeline` is missing. (Context: this runs unattended in a CI job; no one will answer questions. CONDUCTOR_SERVER_URL=https://acme.orkesconductor.com/api, CONDUCTOR_AUTH_KEY and CONDUCTOR_AUTH_SECRET are set as CI secrets. `conductor` v0.1.9 from npm is on PATH; it has no `create-app` command. No saved profiles.)
expected_behavior: Step 1: Resolve the CLI with `ensure-cli.sh` (no `--need`): the v0.1.9 CLI on PATH is accepted, so there is no install question
Step 2: Server choice: `CONDUCTOR_SERVER_URL` is set, so use it; don't default to Developer Edition and don't ask which server
Step 3: Credentials are already injected: check only that CONDUCTOR_AUTH_KEY / CONDUCTOR_AUTH_SECRET are set (names, never values), set CONDUCTOR_SERVER_TYPE=Enterprise if needed
Step 4: No `conductor create-app`, no browser approval, no `ensure-cli --need create-app`
Step 5: Run `conductor workflow list --json`, look for `order_pipeline`, and exit non-zero (or report failure) if it's missing
success_criteria: Uses CONDUCTOR_SERVER_URL and the injected CONDUCTOR_AUTH_* variables as the connection
Does not run `conductor create-app` or ask for any browser approval
Accepts the existing CLI on PATH; does not ask to install a newer CLI or require `create-app`
Never stops to ask the user a question (the job is unattended)
Never prints credential values, runs `env`, enables shell tracing, or puts credentials in command arguments
Lists workflows with a real CLI call and checks for `order_pipeline`
